texts.preamble: M/S. Sri Krishna Water Tech vs The Designated Officer on 1 December, 2016
texts.facts: The petitioners in these batch of writ petitions are engaged in manufacture and sale of packaged drinking water in water bottles, plastics cans and/or pouches as the case may be. The officials attached to the office of the first respondent have caused inspection of the manufacturing facility of the petitioners herein on various dates, issued stop sale notice in some cases.
texts.arguments: In some other cases, after issuing such stop sale notices, without any further notice, the manufacturing facility was sealed by the officials by either citing sub-standard of water or misbranding of water and in some cases the water sumples tested are unsafe for human consumption. 2. The learned counsel appearing for the respective petitioners, in unison, would contend that the sealing of the premises by the respondents is illegal inasmuch as before sealing the premises, the petitioners were not given any notice. Even though the petitioners have complied with various defects pointed out by the respondents at the time of inspection, without considering the same, the respondents have sealed the premises in violation of principles of natural justice. According to the learned counsel for the respective petitioners, even assuming if there is any violation of the procedures prescribed under The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as "The Act") committed by the petitioners, under the said Act, they have a right to show improvement. After making the necessary improvement, the petitioners will get a chance to subject their samples for testing before the accredited and/or authorised central government agency for obtaining necessary certificate. Therefore, without seeking any further clarification or proof with regard to improvement, if any, made by the petitioners and without giving any further notice or opportunity, the respondents have sealed the premises. By reason of the sealing of the manufacturing facility of the petitioners, their entire business activities have come to a grinding halt and it had eroded into their right to carry on business. Further, the machineries installed by the petitioners, which are kept inside the business premises, will lose their utility value if the sealing of the premises continues. Therefore, the learned counsel for the petitioners, in unison, prayed this Court to issue appropriate direction to the respondents to remove the seal and permit the petitioners to carry out general maintenance work and to engage in manufacture of water only for testing purpose and not otherwise. M/S. Sri Krishna Water Tech vs The Designated Officer on 1 December, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38523941/ 2 3. In most of the cases, the petitioners have filed an affidavit of undertaking to the effect that if the seal is removed and the premises is permitted to open, they will only carry on general maintenance work and manufacture water only for the purpose of testing. It is specifically undertaken by the petitioners that they will not engage in manufacture and sale of water for commercial purpose or they will resort to sell the existing stock of water for commercial purpose. The petitioners have given a solemn undertaking that if the premises is ordered to be de-sealed, they will comply with all the defects pointed out by the respondents and only after getting necessary permission from the respondents they will resort to engage in sale of water for commercial purpose. It is also specifically undertaken by the petitioners that they will cooperate with the respondents and will ensure compliance of all the procedural formalities. The petitioners have also undertaken to have their facility inspected by the officials of the respondents so that the compliances made by the petitioners can be considered by the respondents before passing further order. 4. The learned Additional Advocate General appearing for the respondents would contend that the respondents have strictly followed the procedures contemplated under the Act before sealing the manufacturing facility of the petitioners. The sealing of the premises has become inevitable inasmuch as the products manufactured by the petitioners are unsafe for human consumption and it will result in adverse health consequences on the livelihood of the consumers. Further, in some of the cases, the petitioners, by violating the procedures contemplated under the Act have engaged in selling their products by "misbranding" and in some cases the product sold by the petitioners were sub-standard. In such circumstances, in order to ensure the safety and well being of the citizens, the respondents have rightly resorted to closure of the manufacturing facility of the petitioners. The learned Additional Advocate General appearing for the respondents also relied on Clause 2.10.8 of The Food Safety and Standards (Food Addictives) Regulation, 2011 wherein it was stated that the packaged drinking water shall confirm to certain characteristics features such as colour, taste, tubidity etc., According to the learned Additional Advocate General as the products manufactured by the petitioners did not meet the above specifications, the respondents have resorted to seal the premises of the manufacturing facility of the petitioners. It is also further brought to the notice of this Court by the learned Additional Advocate General that the Green Triobunal has directed the authorities concerned to resort to closure of the facility if there is any violation of the procedures contemplated under the Act. The learned Additional Advocate General therefore justified the action of the respondents in closing the manufacturing facility of the petitioners and he prayed for dismissal of the writ petitions. 5. I heard the learned counsel appearing for the respective petitioners and the learned Additional Advocate General appearing for the respondents. The main contentions urged on behalf of the petitioners is that the closure of the manufacturing facility by the respondents is illegal inasmuch as it is not preceded by any notice. Therefore, according to the petiitoners, the action of the respondents in closing the manufacturing facility of the respective petitioners is in violation of the principles of natural justice. Even if there is any violation committed by the petitioners in not complying with the procedures laid down under the Act, it will not give any right to the respondents to resort to closure of the manufacturing facility of the petitioners without following due process of law. According to the counsel for the petitioners, even as per the Act, if there is any violation committed by the manufacturers, action has to be taken for closure of the manufacturing facility M/S. Sri Krishna Water Tech vs The Designated Officer on 1 December, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38523941/ 3 only by following the due process in accordance with law, meaning thereby, before resorting to such action, a notice has to be given to the petitioners and in the absence of the same, the action taken by the respondents is contrary to the provisions of the Act besides being violative of principles of natural justice. 6. At the same time, the learned Additional Advocate General appearing for the respondents brought to the notice of this Court that closure of the manufacturing facility of the petitioners has become inevitable inasmuch as after inspection, it was found that the products manufactured by the petitioners are either sub-standard, mis-branded or in some cases, it is unsafe for human consumption. In such event, allowing the petitioners to continue their business without complying with the mandatory procedures contemplated under the Act would jeopardise the consumers especially in some cases, it was found that the products manufactured by the petitioners is unsafe for human consumption. I therefore find force in the said submission of the learned counsel appearing for the respective petitioners that before resorting to sealing the manufacturing facility of the petitioners, the respondents ought to have issued a notice or given an opportunity of hearing to them. Admittedly, the respondents have not issued any notice to the petitioners. Therefore, the enmasse sealing of the manufacturing facility of the petitioners, without following the principles of natural justice by the respondents is liable to be interfered with. However, the learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the petitioners have complied with all the defects pointed out by the respondents during their inspection and in some cases, the petitioners have also tested their product with the accredited labs or agencies appointed by the Central Government. Therefore, according to the petitioners, if the seal is removed and an inspection is conducted by the respondents, they will be in a position to show that they have complied with all the required parameters and that their products are safe for human b consumption. Therefore, it is prayed by the petitioners that the respondents shall be directed to cause an inspection of the manufacturing facility of the petitioners to satisfy themselves as to whether the petitioners have complied with all the procedural requirements and to permit the petitioners to commence commercial sale of their products.
